policy_title: Abolish Business Rates and Introduce Commercial Landowner Levy
stated: Abolish business rates and replace them with a Commercial Landowner Levy to boost small businesses and empower them to create new local jobs, helping high streets.

source.quote: Boost small businesses and empower them to create new local jobs, including by abolishing business rates and replacing them with a Commercial Landowner Levy to help our high streets.

bearing_set.reason: Shifting the tax burden from business occupiers to commercial landowners is designed to reduce operating costs for small businesses, directly bearing on job creation, business viability, and employment quality in local/high-street economies.

Replacing an occupancy-based property tax with a landowner levy removes the disincentive to occupy and improve commercial premises, reducing dead-weight loss and plausibly boosting small business formation, high-street vitality, and aggregate productivity — a real verdict on prosperity and economic dynamism.

Shifting the tax burden from business occupiers (disproportionately smaller, less-wealthy firms) to commercial landowners (disproportionately institutional investors and wealthy individuals) is a genuine redistribution mechanism that could narrow the wealth/income gap, earning a real verdict on inequality.

membership_note: Two clear bearings: the economic-efficiency and aggregate-prosperity effect (O13) and the distributional shift from occupiers to landowners (O14). O4 (job quality/pay) is excluded as the mechanism is employment quantity — an O13 signal. O12 is excluded because the stated intent is revenue-neutral replacement and no concrete funding-gap mechanism is specified. O11 is excluded as business rates are not a household income tax and the household pass-through is too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
